title: Prawn Fajitas
subtitle: Garlic and lime prawns with sizzling peppers in warm tortillas
excerpt: Raw prawns marinated in cumin, smoked paprika, garlic, and lime, cooked fast in a very hot pan with peppers and onion, served in warm flour tortillas with soured cream and fresh coriander.
sourceNotes: Prawn fajitas: a seafood adaptation of the classic Tex-Mex fajita, widespread on the Gulf Coast of Texas and Mexico. Prawns cook in under 3 minutes and pair well with the standard fajita spice profile. Based on classic American coastal Tex-Mex cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the prawns for up to 30 minutes only. Longer than 1 hour in lime juice starts to cook them chemically (ceviche effect). Cook just before serving.

content.text: Prawn fajitas are the fastest of the fajita variations: the prawns need only 2-3 minutes in a very hot pan. The risk is overcooking. Prawns become rubbery quickly when heat is overdone. Cook them last, after the peppers are finished. Watch for the colour change from grey-pink to opaque pink all the way through, then get them out of the pan immediately.

items.prepNote: raw king prawns, defrosted if frozen, peeled and deveined
mashed with lime juice and salt

content.text: Marinate the prawns for 15-30 minutes only. Lime juice begins to denature the proteins in prawns (the ceviche effect) if left longer than an hour; they will feel pre-cooked and go rubbery in the pan.
Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, lime juice, half the olive oil, and salt. Toss the prawns in the mixture. Leave to marinate for 15-30 minutes.

Heat the remaining oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onions and cook for 5 minutes. Add the peppers and cook for 5-6 minutes until soft with charred edges. Season with salt. Set aside.

Turn the heat to high. Lay the prawns in a single layer in the pan. Cook for 1-1.5 minutes until pink and just opaque on the underside. Flip and cook for 30-60 seconds on the other side. They are done when fully pink and opaque throughout.
Add the peppers and onions back to the pan and toss briefly to warm through. Serve immediately in warm tortillas with soured cream, mashed avocado, coriander, and lime wedges.

items.cause: Overcooked, or marinated in lime juice too long
items.fix: Prawns cook in under 2 minutes per side. Pull them from the heat the moment they're fully opaque. Marinate for no more than 30 minutes.

items.symptom: Prawns release a lot of liquid and steam rather than sear
items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or prawns not properly defrosted and dried
items.fix: If using frozen prawns, defrost fully and pat dry before marinating. The pan should be smoking hot before the prawns go in.

items.symptom: Prawns cook unevenly — some done, some raw
items.cause: Different sizes in the same batch, or laid over each other
items.fix: Sort prawns by size if very mixed, or cook in two batches. They need to be in a single layer to cook evenly.

items.symptom: Too little filling for four tortillas each
items.cause: 500g prawns looks more than it is after cooking
items.fix: Prawns shrink considerably during cooking. Make sure the peppers are generous; they're as much the filling as the prawns.

content.text: Prawn fajitas come from the Gulf Coast of Texas and Mexico, where prawns are plentiful and the Tex-Mex fajita format suits a quick seafood supper. They work well for dinner parties because the cook time is so short that everything finishes at once. The marinade does the seasoning; the pan needs to be very hot to get any colour on the prawns before they overcook.
